case-studies.title: Engineering case studies
case-studies.description: Systems I designed and built. Clients are not identified.

credit-ai.title: Credit analysis and AI automation
credit-ai.summary: A credit analysis module for an FIDC securitization company, with engines that query bureaus and read documents, and a robot that captures delivery receipts and validates them with AI before writing them off in the ERP.

highlights.1: Analysis engines run in rounds that the analyst starts, continues or stops from the interface, with failures logged and coverage per engine.
highlights.2: AI validation of receipts with configurable model fallback and effort: what the model refuses goes to human review and what it approves is written off in the ERP.
highlights.3: A TypeScript scraper with a queue and worker, a paid bureau refresh with a concurrency lock, and end-to-end tests with simulators for the AI and the ERP.

payments.title: A payments platform with 21 services
payments.summary: A payments system split into Node and Java services, wired straight into partner banks, with web and mobile products running on top of those same services.

highlights.1: Domain split into independent services (IAM, wallet, orders, payments, receivables, tax, notifications) with distinct gateways for the admin console and the end customer.
highlights.2: Dedicated Java/Spring services for Pix, bank slips, receivables, and invoice issuing, isolating each banking integration from the product core.
highlights.3: A Next.js console and a React Native app on the same services, with CI/CD on Docker, PM2, and GitHub Actions.

edtech.title: White-label apps for schools
edtech.summary: A single codebase produces independent apps per institution. Branding, bundle, integrations and features all come from tenant configuration.

highlights.1: A tenant registry driving both build time (bundle ID, icon, splash) and runtime (theme, LMS URL, feature flags) from one source.
highlights.2: Continuous Android and iOS releases with Expo/EAS plus OTA updates triggered by pushes to the main branch.
highlights.3: NestJS backends covering auth, cloud files, push, and email, alongside Next.js admin consoles and the Ionic/Angular mobile LMS.

spectroscopy.title: Botanical identification SaaS driven by spectroscopy
spectroscopy.summary: A platform wiring a near-infrared scanner to statistical identification models, with the same interface running in the browser and on the desktop.

highlights.1: A Next.js PWA as the single source of UI, also packaged inside a Tauri/Rust desktop shell that bridges the hardware.
highlights.2: NestJS microservices behind a single gateway, with per-institution data isolation through PostgreSQL row level security.
highlights.3: A monorepo with its own design system, typed HTTP contracts, and Storybook as the living UI reference.

realestate.title: Real-estate SaaS platform
realestate.summary: CRM, operations, property catalog, and client portal on a multi-tenant microservice architecture.

highlights.1: NestJS services communicating over gRPC behind an API Gateway, with contracts versioned in a shared package.
highlights.2: Domain modeling for properties, deals, and brokers, with per-tenant authorization and data isolation.
highlights.3: A pnpm + Turborepo monorepo whose domain, UI, and config packages are reused across backend and frontend.

ritmar.title: Ritmar: multi-tenant management for academies
ritmar.summary: My own product, from zero to production: enrollments, classes, graduations, recurring billing and POS, with a public website per school.

highlights.1: Recurring billing via Pix and card with one gateway per school, idempotent webhooks, reconciliation and an audit trail.
highlights.2: Per-tenant isolation in PostgreSQL and a public website per subdomain or custom domain, with indexing controlled by tenant status (robots, noindex and sitemap).
highlights.3: Full operation: implantation sales flow, per-school provisioning and Docker delivery with encrypted backups and scheduled billing routines.

ai-workflow.title: AI in the engineering workflow
ai-workflow.description: I put AI at the center of the process. The engineering workflow runs around agents and is held to the same rigor as any system in production.

spec-driven.title: Spec and plan before code
spec-driven.description: Any change of substance starts from a spec with the problem, constraints and acceptance criteria, and from a plan in verifiable tasks. Fixing an ambiguous spec costs less than fixing thirty files later.

orchestration.title: Each phase on the right model
orchestration.description: Planning, implementing, debugging and reviewing call for different models. Each phase goes to the one that performs best on it, and whoever writes the plan does not implement it.

context.title: Project standards, versioned
context.description: Module layout, logging and testing conventions live in the repository and go through PRs like any code. A new agent inherits the rule instead of guessing.

tooling.title: Tooling over a protocol
tooling.description: The agent reads tasks, the database, the browser and CI over MCP, without relying on context pasted by hand.

verification.title: Evidence before claims
verification.description: The test fails before the implementation, and lint, typecheck, coverage and end-to-end runs in CI act as the gate. A flaky test gets rewritten, never ignored.

review.title: Human review at the merge
review.description: I read everything the agent returns before opening the PR. It speeds up the right code and the wrong code, and the gain is in the gates that catch it early.

ai-workflow.footnote: I applied this to real products: I moved a six-person squad to a spec-driven flow in edtech, and today I build a microservice SaaS platform for the real estate market.

details.1: End-to-end credit analysis module on the internal platform (React and NestJS): a dashboard by risk pillars, overall score, opinion, committee minutes and PDF reports, an economic group map with per-node detail, and an audit trail.
details.2: Credit analysis engines run in rounds that the analyst starts, continues or stops from the interface: bureau queries, financial indicators extracted from statements, a relationship map and a visit report, with some engines reading documents with AI.
details.3: On-demand paid credit bureau refresh, with a per-company concurrency lock, immediate refusal of simultaneous requests, and a record of who asked and who is billed.
details.4: A robot that captures delivery receipts from a third-party portal: a TypeScript scraper with domain and infrastructure layers, token authentication and a health endpoint, plus a queue and worker on the platform.
details.5: AI validation of the receipts: a model with configurable fallback and effort, images resized before sending, refusals routed to human review, and automatic write-off in the ERP when a receipt is approved.
details.6: An access layer for the financial ERP on SQL Server, with caching and degraded reads when the database does not respond.
details.7: End-to-end tests with Playwright, simulators for the scraper, the AI and the ERP, and a local Docker stack, to run the full flow without depending on production.
